status: PERSISTENCE NOT VERIFIED: final stable read-only full-flash probe found the candidate data word at 0x1F744 still erased. After probe reset the VIA test slot reads 0x0001. The only candidate-area bytes differing from the pre-test image are at 0x1F408..0x1F40C. Probe snapshots, bootloader, outside-application flash, and hidden metadata all match. No erase or program command was sent during the probe.

candidate_page_gate_clear_fix_20261104.finding: The recovered vendor program stub clears only the selected page-gate bit with a read-modify-write (LDR, BIC, STR). The QMK driver instead wrote zero to the whole gate register after each operation.
candidate_page_gate_clear_fix_20261104.change: Both erase and program paths now use *gate &= ~bit, matching the recovered stub while preserving other page-gate bits.

stock_firmware.captured_settings_protocol: Vendor SetMatrix (0xA0) traffic writes the complete four-layer keymap; see ranked_re.db remap_capture and setmatrix_format.
stock_firmware.storage_location_and_runtime_save_load_p: Application flash-controller routines and the SetMatrix save path are traced in firmware_dump/application_thumb_linear.txt. The stock matrix handler writes four keymap layers as paired 512-byte pages: layer 1 D5-D6, layer 2 D7-D8, layer 3 D9-DA, layer 4 DB-DC. The stock reset-default path erases D5-DF.
stock_firmware.separate_bootloader_persistence: Firmware COMPLETE updates a separate 512-byte hidden metadata block at CPU address 0x10000600; this does not establish that ordinary keymap/VIA settings use that block.

current_backend: The page-gate clear correction matches the recovered vendor stub, but it did not make persistent VIA reliable. A stable read-only full-flash probe confirmed the reported address 0x1F744 is erased; only three candidate-area bytes at 0x1F408..0x1F40C differ from the pre-test image. After the probe reset, VIA layer 2,row 4,column 9 reads 0x0001. Investigate controller address encoding, QMK wear-leveling offset semantics, or actual runtime address before any further write.
erase_program_driver: experimental custom QMK driver linked in the candidate build and exercised in one controlled live persistence attempt; writes are restricted to pages F8-FF. The controller diagnostic reported success, but the read-only raw dump disagreed with its reported address, so the backend is not accepted.

decision: Do not open a PR or claim persistent VIA. The final read-only hardware probe is stable and passed, but persistence failed: the VIA slot reads 0x0001 after the probe reset and the diagnostic-reported location 0x1F744 is erased. Preserve current firmware and investigate address mapping offline before another controlled write. No erase/program command was sent by the final probe.

Raw flash contents do not match the runtime-reported programmed address; persistence is unverified.

controller_root_cause_evidence.confidence: strong candidate; requires physical re-test after fix
controller_root_cause_evidence.vendor_stub_program_sequence: firmware_dump/vendor_stub_recovered.bin disassembly: 0x2000009A sets one-hot page gate at 0x400130D0 + 4*(page>>5), performs DATA/ADDR/CR and polls status, then clears that gate at 0x200000CC.
controller_root_cause_evidence.vendor_stub_timing: at 48 MHz, vendor stub writes 216000 (0x34BC0*48/48) to controller offset 0x3C and 1440000 (0x15F900*48/48) to offset 0x40.
controller_root_cause_evidence.candidate_source_updated: platforms/ry72xx/drivers/wear_leveling/wear_leveling_nova_flash.c now sets and clears the page gate around each operation and uses 0x34BC0 timing at offset 0x3C.
controller_root_cause_evidence.corrected_hardware_test: The selected-bit page-gate clear candidate was flashed and verified. The live diagnostic reported stage 5 at QMK offset 0x744/page FB and claimed physical word 0xFB63FEF7; the user confirmed the test value 0x0004 after one cold restart. Final read-only probe then produced identical pre/post 128 KiB dumps, but the expected CPU address 0x1F744 was erased and only three bytes at 0x1F408..0x1F40C differed from the verified pre-test candidate image. After the probe returned the app, raw VIA GET_KEYCODE read 0x0001. This disproves reliable persistence for this candidate; controller address/result verification is inconsistent.
controller_root_cause_evidence.page_gate_mismatch: Before correction, backend checked 0x400130D0+group*4 but never set the selected one-hot page bit or cleared it after completion.
controller_root_cause_evidence.timing_mismatch: Before correction, offsets 0x3C and 0x40 both used 0x15F900; the recovered stub uses 0x34BC0 at 0x3C and 0x15F900 at 0x40.
controller_root_cause_evidence.runtime_diagnostic: Raw HID read-only diagnostic showed page FA permission word 0xFFFFFFFF and gate register readback 0xFFFFFFFF. Backend stage 2 rejected at page_allowed before controller command; controller status stayed 0 and physical word stayed 0xFFFFFFFF. Immediate VIA set still updated runtime cache to 0x0004.
controller_root_cause_evidence.current_source_correction: page_allowed now requires only the per-page metadata permission bit (and fixed F8-FF bounds). The gate register is set/cleared around the operation but its all-ones readback is not treated as a precondition.

diagnostic_read_20261103.finding: The driver treated a one-hot gate register readback of 0xFFFFFFFF as a busy/precondition bit. The recovered vendor stub does not read-check this register before a write; it overwrites it with the one-hot page mask and clears it afterward. Metadata permission is 0xFFFFFFFF, so permission allows the page.
diagnostic_read_20261103.source_correction: page_allowed now checks only the metadata permission bit and still enforces F8-FF bounds; operation sets/clears the recovered gate as before.
